sources.title: Original JSON and fixed-material CPU contract audit
Fixed-material deterministic-topic shortcut counterexample
sources.details: For fixed notice N, all-lines target T_all differs from Chinese-only target T_zh. A response rule f(N) independent of request returns one target and cannot equal both; retaining both pairs makes the request-relevant distinction explicit. It does not prove a trained model generalizes or cannot use any other shortcut.

claims.statement: SFT training examples must retain the current request in the conditioning input and pair it with a target that performs the request; a four-line target after Chinese-only teaches the wrong task despite copying true source phrases.
claims.location: course/chapters/08.md#8.15 paragraphs beginning 如果想用示範 and supplementary §3.1–3.2/§2.1,§4.3 references
claims.scope: Supervised input-target relationship and concrete finite notice task; does not claim a few examples guarantee learning arbitrary formats or that each new phrasing requires a dedicated sample.

evidence.locator: §3.1 Step1 p6; §3.2 pp6–7 SFT labeler demonstrations
evidence.supports: Supervised fine-tuning uses demonstrations of desired output behavior on input prompts.

evidence.locator: §2.1 p3 tasks/templates and Figure4; §4.3 p7 role of instructions
evidence.supports: Natural-language task templates are included with target outputs and instruction presence has an explicit role in the cited method.

claims.statement: Keeping the same notice under both all-copy and Chinese-only requests makes the request-dependent difference explicit; topic alone cannot determine both distinct required outputs.
claims.location: 8.15 paragraph 保留這種同材料對照
claims.scope: Logical removal of this specific topic-to-output ambiguity from the displayed pair design; no trained-model shortcut elimination, measured causal performance effect, or guarantee of generalization.

evidence.locator: f(N) cannot equal distinct T_all and T_zh for one fixed N
evidence.supports: Shows why a topic-only deterministic target rule is insufficient for these paired required outputs.

evidence.locator: §4.3 p7 Role of instructions; §2.1 p3 instruction/target relation
evidence.supports: Supports task instructions as meaningful conditioning, not the claim that one pair trains a model successfully.
Actual output construction preserves the same notice bytes for all selection and format cases.

claims.statement: The fixed four-row notice yields four original-order lines for all-copy, two Chinese lines from rows1/3, two English lines from rows2/4, and the third request target is a single text field containing the ordered Chinese string list. The referenced two-branch SVG agrees.
claims.location: 8.15 material and request/target tables, JSON fence, exercise, referenced SVG
claims.scope: Exact hand-authored material and target mapping; counts are notice rows/lines, not trained-model scores or neural-token counts. SVG depicts the first two requests only.

evidence.locator: contract-results.json material_rows/selection_cases; original_fence_sha256; English request counterexample
evidence.supports: Executed exact original JSON plus table-derived fixed-material mapping and English-request variants.

evidence.locator: §1 array ordered-sequence definition; §2 JSON-text grammar; §4 object; §5 array; §7 Unicode strings
evidence.supports: Confirms the displayed one-field JSON object is standard syntax and its array can preserve required line order.

verification.expected: All-copy rows[1,2,3,4]=4 lines; Chinese rows[1,3]=2; English rows[2,4]=2. Original JSON {text:[今日休館,明日開放]} with only text key, string list and preserved order.
verification.observed: Exact selection_line_counts 4/2/2 and row selections asserted; original JSON schema and scope both True. Native rendered SVG viewed: four shared lines and targets of four versus two lines, correct two branch arrows.
verification.details: Derived selections from current source table, parsed untouched raw JSON fence, checked English exercise and unchanged-Chinese-under-English failure; figure actually rendered in Inkscape and viewed.
verification.tolerance: Exact equality for row IDs, line counts, Unicode strings and ordering; no floating-point tolerance or percentage denominator applies.

claims.statement: New wording of a request on the same notice tests a different generalization scope from a new notice/request combination; related notice variants must remain one family when asserting unseen-material evaluation.
claims.location: 8.15 paragraph 檢查新題時 and supplementary FLAN evaluation boundary
claims.scope: Evaluation design and held-out scope only; no new model evaluation was run, and rewording the trained material is not declared unseen material. FLAN holds out task clusters, not this specific notice family.

evidence.supports: Dependent domain-specific groups must be absent from paired training to evaluate unseen groups.

evidence.locator: §3.2 p6 long common-prefix deduplication and train/validation/test by userID
evidence.supports: Original paper explicitly defines grouping and separates held-out sources; does not prescribe the notice task grouping itself.
Unseen-task claims depend on an explicit holdout definition; quoted FLAN clusters are distinct from notice-family holdouts.

claims.statement: The original JSON fence and necessary short fixed-material variants meet or fail the specified scope/format contract exactly as stated. Local render_chat retains material+request, supervises assistant bytes plus EOS at the shifted prediction positions; removing EOS leaves an incomplete stopping target even when other answer targets remain.
claims.location: 8.15 JSON fence, Chinese/English format comparison, EOS supervision sentence and linked7.3/7.4/7.9 contract
claims.scope: Single explicit coverage claim for related JSON API/basic syntax and actual local data contracts: original JSON and manual targets, 11 counterexamples, 6 CPU render_chat/pad_batch examples. No Python fence exists in8.15; no model training, gradient, update, generated reply or ability score was performed.

evidence.supports: Original JSON parse and explicit strict schema checks are real CPython operations; schema is specified by the task.

evidence.locator: ByteTokenizer lines15–24; render_chat lines54–68; pad_batch lines71–86
evidence.supports: Exact byte encoding, input retention, assistant answer+EOS mask, once-shifted labels and truncation behavior.
Repository expects already-shifted labels and distinguishes EOS stopping from a hard limit; no model execution claimed.
Official documentation supports causal sequence and training response boundary structure, with model-specific control formats.
